Every strategic exception needs CFO delegate approval regardless of the resulting margin. Pricing below the 20% minimum, including the merchant's requested 1.58% + $0.12, is only possible with this approval.","policy_evidence_id":"PRC-2026.1§7"}],"decision":"counter_offer","explanation":"The decision date is 2026-07-15, so policy PRC-2026.1 applies. Merchant-specific cost data is available: 1.40% + $0.05 per transaction.

The merchant's requested 1.58% + $0.12 is the merchant's own unverified statement. At that price, monthly revenue would be $77,100 against a cost of $65,500. That gives a gross margin of 15.05%, which is below the 20% enterprise minimum. It is also a 24.41% discount vs list ($102,000 per month at 2.10% + $0.15). Pricing below the minimum margin is prohibited unless an approved strategic exception applies. The co-brand exception has been requested but not approved.

We therefore counter at 1.69% + $0.12 per transaction, keeping the merchant's requested per-transaction fee:
- Revenue: $82,050 per month
- Cost: $65,500 per month
- Gross profit: $16,550 per month
- Gross margin: 20.17%, which meets the 20% minimum
- Discount vs list: 19.56%

This price still requires two approvals:
- Deal desk, because monthly volume is above $4,000,000.
- Regional pricing manager, because the discount exceeds 12%.

Because a strategic exception is formally on file, a CFO delegate must also approve or close it out. If leadership wants to grant the full request, that is only possible as an approved strategic exception with CFO delegate sign-off.

No promotion applies.
